recentWork.title: A modular foundation for knowledge and document extraction.
recentWork.summary: The template combines OCR for scanned documents, adaptive field extraction, and built-in authentication. Teams can tailor its modules and extraction schemas to their use case, while developers can access enterprise knowledge through controlled MCP integrations.
recentWork.detail: Adaptive extraction uses LangGraph and LangChain to build schema-driven retrieval queries for each requested field. It retrieves relevant chunks from ChromaDB, reranks them by similarity, and constructs an LLM prompt with source material. Results include the field value, supporting context, page number, and model-reported confidence. Subsequent retrieval passes target only unresolved fields, keeping repeated context and unnecessary model input down.
recentWork.outcome: A reusable, configurable foundation for enterprise knowledge and document extraction, adopted for a contract-field extraction application.
recentWork.intro: A shared foundation for enterprise knowledge use cases, extended to coding agents with controlled access.
recentWork.context: Designed a reusable knowledge-management template for document extraction, internal knowledge search, and termsheet comparison. Adopted as the account standard, it has also been used by another team to implement contract-field extraction.
recentWork.notes: Vertical slice architecture keeps ingestion modules independently removable; environment variables can disable modules such as Jira ingestion. The template supports enterprise authentication through Kerberos and JWT-based API keys. Its MCP integration makes knowledge available in Claude Code and Copilot CLI, with group-based authorisation and time-limited credentials.
recentWork.recognition: Recognised in the CIO newsletter in 2026 for the knowledge-management template, adopted for contract-field extraction.

capabilities.title: Extraction that follows the missing fields
capabilities.body: Retrieves and reranks source chunks for the requested schema, then returns field values with context, page references, and confidence. Further passes focus on fields still missing.

capabilities.title: Reusable presets or on-demand schemas
capabilities.body: Teams can extend predefined extraction presets or define field names, data types, validation rules, and examples on the fly to try a new document use case.

capabilities.title: Modules teams can tailor
capabilities.body: Teams can disable or remove ingestion modules without carrying unnecessary functionality. The modular design includes OCR for scanned documents and built-in authentication.

recentWork.title: Taking applications from implementation to production.
recentWork.context: An infrastructure dashboard gave stakeholders valuable visibility into their applications, but its underlying design was difficult to maintain and prepare for production.
recentWork.summary: I reviewed the Python and React codebase and defined a phased modernisation plan. The restructured backend and React application are now deployed on Rancher. Work continues on a scheduled data pipeline and database-backed storage.
recentWork.detail: After reviewing the codebase with its developer, I broke the work into phases: separate frontend and backend responsibilities, restructure the Python code, remove spreadsheet dependencies, and replace direct consumption of generated JSON files with REST endpoints. The planned next stage uses Prefect flows to collect data into SQL, with the Python API serving it to React.
recentWork.intro: Building the service, improving the codebase, and carrying the work through deployment.
recentWork.outcome: The dashboard has a better-structured codebase, with its React application and Python API deployed on Rancher. The Prefect and SQL data pipeline remains planned.

recentWork.title: Taking PDF clause extraction into production.
recentWork.context: An existing PDF clause-extraction application had a Python RAG backend and React interface, but needed substantial code and deployment improvements before it could run reliably in production.
recentWork.summary: I modernised the codebase, resolved deployment issues, and established a repeatable build and release process. This included adapting document processing and model delivery to the firm’s environment. The application was successfully deployed on Rancher and has run reliably in production for about a year.
recentWork.detail: The Python RAG service uses Tesseract OCR and FAISS. I adapted OCR for Linux and moved the application onto GitLab CI. Because Hugging Face was blocked, I packaged the embedding model from Nexus into the application container. These changes addressed application and environment issues that were preventing production deployment.
recentWork.intro: Improving an existing clause-extraction application and carrying it through a successful production release.
recentWork.outcome: Successfully deployed on Rancher and running reliably in production for about a year.
recentWork.recognition: Recognised in the CIO newsletter for contributions to the clause-extraction application’s production delivery.

recentWork.title: Encoding deployment conventions into onboarding.
recentWork.summary: Replaced manual deployment-template setup with a guided onboarding skill. It prepares and validates the configuration needed to deploy services to Rancher, and supports later service additions.
recentWork.detail: The skill turns service requirements into application charts, infrastructure charts, and Flux configuration. It creates the required repositories and branches, validates the setup with Helm and Kubernetes tooling, and publishes it using the firm’s deployment conventions.
recentWork.outcome: Service onboarding and subsequent additions follow the same configuration, repository and validation workflow.
recentWork.intro: Replacing repeated template editing with a guided workflow that follows the firm’s deployment conventions.

recentWork.title: From Informatica workflows to Python and Prefect.
recentWork.summary: Built a migration plugin that takes Informatica workflows from discovery and assessment to equivalent Python/Prefect code. It supports application-wide planning and retains progress across runs.
recentWork.detail: The plugin separates discovery, assessment and code generation into focused skills. Discovery accepts manual evidence or Informatica XML exports and records missing behaviour and unresolved references. Assessment examines complexity and commonality across workflows. Generated code follows the firm’s Python project structure and AutoSys, Rancher and Prefect conventions. Each skill’s progress is tracked in JSON so the process can continue across runs.
recentWork.notes: The discovery step keeps extracted metadata, assumptions and missing runtime details explicit. Parameter files, scheduler details, production run history and SME notes provide additional context when available for downstream assessment and code generation.
recentWork.outcome: A connected migration process with workflow findings, executive reporting, generated implementations, and retained progress.
recentWork.intro: Taking legacy workflows through discovery and migration planning to equivalent Python/Prefect code.

recentWork.title: An API for financial data.
recentWork.summary: Built a Python API exposing financial data, with a structured implementation the team could extend. Explained the architecture and development conventions during handover.
recentWork.detail: Separated request handling, business logic, and data access to make the service easier to maintain and extend. The implementation uses FastAPI and SQLAlchemy with Oracle.
recentWork.outcome: A financial data API and a shared reference for continued development.
recentWork.intro: Making financial data available through an API, with a working implementation and clear conventions for the team.

recentWork.title: Unblocking browser automation on Rancher.
recentWork.summary: Unblocked a regulatory scraping application by getting its browser runtime working on Rancher.
recentWork.detail: Used the official Playwright container and resolved deployment and connectivity issues so the Crawl4AI application could use the browser in the Kubernetes environment.
recentWork.outcome: The team had a working browser runtime for its scraping application.
recentWork.intro: Removing a browser-runtime blocker from a team’s regulatory scraping workflow.

recentWork.title: A prototype hub for organising our tools.
recentWork.summary: Prototyped a shared home for custom skills, MCP integrations, and modernisation reporting. The aim is to make these resources easier to find while keeping each tool as a separate application.
recentWork.detail: Used Vite module federation to keep the tools independently modular within a configurable shell. The hub brings together GitLab-hosted skills, MCP integrations, and modernisation reporting. I built the initial reporting module using ServiceNow data; other developers have since extended it.
recentWork.outcome: An organisational prototype for finding and accessing internal engineering tools.
recentWork.intro: A prototype to bring scattered engineering resources into one place.

recentWork.title: Making business data accessible through an API.
recentWork.summary: Built a .NET API over existing business data that other teams previously had no API to access. Carried the service from implementation through deployment on Rancher.
recentWork.detail: Built a .NET and Entity Framework Core API over existing SQL Server tables and views, making business data accessible to other teams. I prepared its Helm and Flux configuration using the onboarding skill and deployed it to Rancher.

recentWork.title: Reducing memory usage in financial-data APIs.
recentWork.summary: Reduced the memory footprint of existing financial-data APIs through LINQ query optimisation and related implementation changes.
